title: The Lane Chronicle: Four Centuries in Code and Voice
subtitle: 2.5-minute 16:9 featurette · HeyGen ancestors + 1891 register codes

beats.label: 1891 Book
beats.title: The 1891 volume opens
beats.evidence: Lane Genealogies, Vol. I (Exeter, N.H., 1891) · PDF p. 4 · plate p4-i0
beats.teleprompter: In eighteen ninety-one, Jacob Chapman and James Fitts printed Volume One of Lane Genealogies in Exeter, New Hampshire. Inside its pages, a nineteenth-century register code linked four centuries of New England lives. Today, those pages speak.
beats.narrationText: In eighteen ninety-one, Jacob Chapman and James Fitts printed Volume One of Lane Genealogies in Exeter, New Hampshire. Inside its pages, a nineteenth-century register code linked four centuries of New England lives. Today, those pages speak.

beats.label: William · No. 1
beats.title: Root of the Boston line
beats.evidence: Part I · Family No. 1 · PDF p. 19
beats.teleprompter: Hello. I am William Lane — the Boston line begins with me. Freeman of Massachusetts Bay in sixteen fifty-seven, cordwainer in the town records, husband of Mary, and father of Samuel, who carried our name toward Hadley and Hampton. You are standing at Family Number One — the root of the Lane family tree.

beats.label: Sarah · No. 3
beats.title: Hadley frontier household
beats.evidence: Part I · Family No. 3 · PDF p. 22
beats.teleprompter: Hello. I am Sarah Dickinson — wife of Samuel Lane of Hadley on the Connecticut River frontier. Lane Genealogies records our household under Family Number Three. In seventeen oh four, French and Indian raiders took me and my children captive to Canada. Most of us returned; one daughter remained.

beats.label: Cornet John
beats.title: Chester troop of horse
beats.context: Cornet of horse (1754) & sons at Bennington
beats.teleprompter: Hello. I am Cornet John Lane. Born at Hampton on the New Hampshire seacoast, I made my life at Chester — farmer, tavern-keeper, and militia man. In September seventeen fifty-four, the book records me as Cornet in a troop of horse. My sons carried our name into the Revolution, including officers at Bennington.

beats.label: Mind & Cosmos
beats.title: George G. Lane & Jonathan Homer Lane
beats.evidence: 1819–1880 · Patent Office & U.S. Coast Survey · Popular Science May 1884
beats.registerDetail: George G. Lane · Popular Science Monthly, May 1884
beats.teleprompter: Hello. I am Jonathan Homer Lane. Born in eighteen nineteen, I studied at Phillips Exeter and Yale, and spent my career in Washington on the Coast Survey and at the Patent Office. My mathematical law of the gaseous Sun became the Lane–Emden equation — and in nineteen seventy, a crater on the far side of the Moon was named for our family.

beats.label: 1891 Code
beats.title: Register codes unlock the living graph
beats.context: No. N families · (N) carry-forwards · pedigrees decoded
beats.registerDetail: 180 numbered families · 650 coded people · 567 book links
beats.teleprompter: Every numbered family, carry-forward numeral, and generation superscript in the eighteen ninety-one volume has now been decoded into Postgres. Six hundred and fifty coded people and five hundred and sixty-seven book-verified parent and spouse links connect directly to the printed page.
